status: Opt-in native history lifecycle implemented; all 13 local command gates passed on unchanged compiled inputs; three static pairs are matched, and the orbit residency mismatch excludes it from blind preference. Not production TAA, temporal, visual-preference or full-replacement acceptance; the old host and launch defaults are retained.

scope: Scene-owned RGBA16Float ping-pong colour history plus a previous Depth32Float snapshot.
Resolve encodes after opaque terrain/mesh and motion, before plume/sky/cloud/aurora/UI overlays.
History commits only after a real frame submission; a dropped encoder advances nothing.
Resets: terrain publication, conforming/configuration revision, plant epoch, presentation/lighting revision, view mode, projection, exposure, resize.
Quality tiers: low 2x2 / age 4, medium 3x3 / age 8, high 3x3 / age 32.
HDR/capability fallback: TAA requires HDR, motion vectors and jitter; unsupported capabilities resolve to off with a note.
Separate render.temporal_resolve GPU scope includes history compute, colour copy-back and depth snapshot.

history_policy.weight: age/(age+1) running mean, capped at 1 - min_current_weight (0.95 default)
history_policy.source_validity: Scene alpha >= 1 and depth < 1 seed age one even without a previous camera; masked current surfaces seed age zero. Any zero-age tap in the conservative four-tap bilinear history footprint rejects reuse.
excluded: all rigid meshes, including static plants, while previous object transforms are absent
previous-history lookup where motion is invalid; an eligible current static surface still seeds age one

cost.note: Resize temporarily retains old and new targets; existing HDR/motion/depth allocation is unchanged.

captures.settings_base_toml:
# Project Thessa requested graphics settings.
#
# This file is user intent, not runtime truth. At startup the client expands
# `preset`, then resolves requested values through hardware/backend
# capabilities into `ResolvedGraphicsSettings` (see `crates/graphics`):
#
#   graphics.toml -> requested -> preset expansion -> capability resolution
#                  -> ResolvedGraphicsSettings -> renderer + perf metadata
#
# The future GUI edits THIS file (typed editor over the same TOML), never a
# second independent settings system. Unknown future keys are ignored by older
# builds; physics and world state are never affected by this file.
#
# Ray tracing is experimental (legacy Bevy Solari / native wgpu ray queries).
# `ray_tracing = "local"|"full"`
# requests RT device features and fails fast at startup when the GPU/driver
# cannot provide them. Native `"auto"` resolves against the negotiated adapter;
# the legacy launcher may resolve raster before adapter capabilities are known.

version = 1
preset = "high" # low | medium | high | ultra | custom (auto-shown when values diverge)

[renderer]
terrain_ground_detail = true
surface_quality = "high" # native: low F0 approximation; medium GGX; high normal/MR/AO maps
terrain_normal_maps = true # native primary terrain; false skips normal generation/upload/sampling
# surface_quality low/medium/high filters normal detail with +2/+1/+0 extra mip levels.
# Native terrain: 4/8/16 clear-sky GGX samples at low/medium/high. With clouds,
# use 1/2/4 directions and 1/2/4 march steps, <=1 sun step (shared transport law).
# specular_reflections=false compiles out this term. See docs/69.
specular_reflections = true # material/stellar + sky environment; native scene reflection also requires ray_tracing
shadow_memory_mib = 64 # native 3-star cascade atlas cap; reduces resolution, never geometry
# Native RT also tests opaque scene-object visibility toward each active star
# when [shadows].enabled=true, including when specular_reflections=false.
# Terrain visibility still uses the shared raster atlas; ray distance is capped
# by raytracing.max_distance_m. RT off falls back to that atlas.
backend = "auto" # auto | vulkan | metal | webgpu (dx12 deferred pending ADR)
ray_tracing = "auto" # off | local | full | auto
terrain = "gpu_auto" # cpu | gpu_indexed | gpu_auto | gpu_mesh; mesh -> indexed fallback
terrain_mesh_cells = 24 # CPU middle-field density; adaptive per tile; 8..64
material_storage = "rgba_array" # rgba_array | microstore_compact; compact holds
# microstore-encoded pages in residency and decodes at upload time with identical
# sampling (texture format, mips, filtering); storage/upload tradeoff, never visual
resolution_scale = 1.0
vsync = false
hdr = true # native RGBA16Float + Reinhard to SDR; false is direct LDR, no extra target/pass
bloom = false # bright-light glow; off by default to preserve terrain contrast
auto_exposure = false # AE metering curve untuned; deterministic manual EV for now
exposure_ev100 = 13.0 # manual EV100 when auto_exposure = false
fleet_meshes = true # native retained body meshes; false adds no fleet GPU resources/draws
fleet_quality = "high" # low/medium/high: cull meshes below 8/2/0.5 projected pixels

[terrain_topology]
# Native persistent conforming CBT; false retains regular patches at zero extra cost.
# Low/medium/high: 32768/65536/131072 allocation slots, 1/2/4 update waves,
# projected split area 1024/256/64 px^2, merge at one eighth (hysteresis).
# Shared canonical height/material residency is NOT the geometric LOD.
enabled = false
quality = "high"

[atmosphere]
# Native background and mesh/RT indirect terms share this quality-tiered sky
# field and one GPU publication. Disabling releases the field/background draw;
# HDR uses the shared display pass; native stellar discs use the catalogue pass.
# Native: shared single-scattering/airglow environment for mesh reflections and
# derived diffuse ambient. Low/medium/high grids: 8x4 / 16x8 / 32x16; changed
# inputs refresh at most every 8/4/2 frames. Disabled releases the grid.
# The physical sky background is implemented; aerial perspective, multiple
# scattering and external eclipses remain unported in native; see doc 39.
enabled = true
quality = "high" # low | medium | high (budgets only, never physics)
aerial_perspective = true # horizon haze on: distance fades blue like ISS photos; budgets only
density_scale = 0.3 # visual optical-depth gain; simulation pressure is unchanged
# (0.55 washed terrain contrast: measured +100 shadow lift vs no-atmosphere
# reference; 0.3 keeps the blue sky while restoring ground contrast. Revisit
# when the aerial LUT sampling is refined.)
multiple_scattering = false # single-scattering first slice; LUT/MS later
eclipses = true
multi_star = true
limb_scattering = true
sky_dome = true
stars = true # native distant catalogue + physical source discs, independent of scattering
stars_quality = "high" # 8/16/32 atmospheric transmission samples; same flux/catalogue
ray_steps = 24 # view-march steps for CPU queries (4..128)

[clouds]
# Low-deck volume march + cirrus shell (spec section 10): procedural RGBA
# baked once on CPU; the low deck is marched per-pixel (Beer-Lambert over the
# bake + shader detail, sun self-shadow), cirrus stays a thin shell in both
# paths. CBT tile keys share the terrain LOD address space
# (see tools/worldgen-rocky lod::cbt_node_for_tile).
# Native: the same coverage bake drives spherical decks at 3..6 and 9..10 km,
# depth-clipped composition, terrain/mesh/ocean shadows and reflected rays.
# Low/non-volumetric uses a one-column fallback; medium/high use resolved steps.
# No native stochastic integrator, atmospheric multi-scatter, or cloud RT AS.
enabled = true
quality = "high" # low = 512px bake + shell fallback; medium = 1024px; high = 2048px
volumetric = true # true = march the low deck (medium/high); false = shell impostors
integrator = "march" # "march" = real-time stratified march; "stochastic" = scattering approximation
ray_steps = 24 # view-march steps for the volume path (4..24 used, more capped); shells ignore it
cast_shadows = true # low-deck shadows on terrain: sampled from the same bake
# the shells show (sun-parallax offset, soft alpha shaping); off = free
layers = 2 # 1 = low deck, 2 = low + cirrus (Earth-like high thin ice over cumulus)
coverage = 0.55 # 0 overcast .. 1 clear (shaped: 0.55 reads broken deck with open ocean)
opacity = 0.95
animate = true # differential deck drift; off = static

[night_lights]
# Warm emissive city clusters over inhabited land, gated by the terminator
# in-shader. The mask bakes once at startup from the world's inhabited
# regions (bake resolution only, never simulated activity); off = free.
# Native: cached R8 primary-terrain emission, same regular/conforming consumer;
# intensity=0 also skips mask bake/allocation. No secondary-ray city emission.
enabled = true
quality = "medium" # low = 128x64, medium = 256x128, high = 512x256 mask
intensity = 1.0 # 0..2 emissive gain over the mask

[upper_atmosphere]
airglow = true
aurora = true
aurora_quality = "low" # native 64x32/8-step or 128x64/32-step field; animation is independent
aurora_lighting = false # RT emissive proxy (later)
aurora_intensity = 1.0 # 0..4 emission gain over the analytic oval
aurora_animate = true # slide curtains with sim time; off = static oval

[gas_giant]
# Procedural Nereid/Vesper bands baked once on CPU; no shader, no per-frame cost.
enabled = true
quality = "medium" # low = 512x256, medium = 1024x512, high = 2048x1024
animate_bands = true # slow storm drift; off = static
limb_darkening = true # belt/zone contrast baked into the texture

[engine_plume]
# Field-first plume (docs/38): analytic mean field + RCBT residual (later).
# Low = baked cone impostor (fallback artifact); Medium/High = analytic
# per-pixel Beer-Lambert march. Native samples the actual axial stations
# inside a projected bound and clips against scene depth; legacy uses a ribbon.
# Propulsion models and vehicle assets exist, but the client renderer is not
# wired to their live nozzle state yet; it still supplies provisional X-15
# nozzle/source values. RCBT residual rendering is also future work.
enabled = true
quality = "medium" # low = cone impostor; medium = volume/8 steps; high = volume/14 steps
mach_diamonds = true # visual shock-cell toggle; never changes simulation physics
flicker = true
light = true # field-derived legacy nozzle light; native reports this consumer unavailable

[instruments]
# Native HUD only; legacy Bevy retains its CPU instrument until adapted.
enabled = true
quality = "high" # logical diameter 192/256/320 points, rendered at native DPI
layout = "aircraft" # aircraft | rocket; changes display, never flight control
navball_renderer = "auto" # auto/analytic: texture-free GPU; baked: static R8 grid

[ocean]
# Native render-only linear spectral sea; legacy Bevy keeps its analytic path.
# Explicitly opt in: no field, deformation, textures or FFT work when disabled.
enabled = false
quality = "high" # 32/64/128 samples per band at low/medium/high
wind_speed_m_s = 10.0
wind_direction_rad = 0.0 # same angle in each body-fixed planar spectrum
significant_height_m = 2.0
depth_m = 100.0 # uniform reference, not bathymetry
seed = 17
geometry_patches = 16 # 0..=64; whole near partition falls back if over budget
geometry_distance_m = 300.0 # displacement fades from half radius to radius

[raytracing]
# Participation flags for experimental ray paths. The native mesh consumer
# also admits the resident generated terrain grid and bounded near-ocean waves.
# The single mode switch lives in [renderer] ray_tracing.
terrain = true
vehicles = true
landmarks = false
atmosphere = true # ray-aware transmittance/sky queries where supported
clouds = false
max_distance_m = 500000.0
# Native RT scene: consolidated geometry, hit tables and TLAS instances are
# budgeted here; driver-owned acceleration-structure memory is additional.
# Terrain charges borrowed vertex slots conservatively; an over-budget active
# partition falls back whole to raster instead of dropping arbitrary blockers.
scene_memory_mib = 32
max_instances = 4096
# Specular chain length for object reflections (1 = single mirror bounce).
reflection_bounces = 2
ray_bias_m = 0.01

[shadows]
# Native depth reuse is exact: unchanged light matrices and caster inputs need
# no redraw. Camera origin, geometry/membership and mesh transforms/ranges
# invalidate it; this does not lower resolution or impose a refresh cadence.
# Sun shadow cascade cover for the raster path (RT lighting ignores it).
# Engine default ends at 150 m; planetary cover is explicit here instead
# of magic numbers in the client.
enabled = true
quality = "high" # low | medium | high (expands the numbers below on preset apply)
cascades = 4 # 1..=4
max_distance_m = 12000.0 # far end of cover in metres; first cascade ends at max/40
map_size = 4096 # per-cascade texel grid, power of two 512..=8192
normal_bias_m = 1.5 # normal offset in metres against acne on 32 m mesh cells

[debug]
show_atmosphere_bounds = false
show_rt_proxies = false

[surface_plants]
enabled = true
quality = "high"
understory = true
captures.settings_override: Append [temporal] taa=false|true and quality=medium to the base TOML.
captures.matching_note: CPU preparation/publication timing differences are not scene mismatches. Any material residency mismatch makes the corresponding pair ineligible for blind preference; RGB deltas remain descriptive, not temporal quality metrics.

blind_review.status: prepared from matched pairs; no independent reviewer votes were collected

masked_source_regression.observation: The initial orbit frame exposed duplicated tree silhouettes. Both the corrected diagnostic frame and the final orbit-True.png were inspected without observing those silhouettes; this is implementer inspection of still frames, not independent visual acceptance or a general ghosting bound. Streaming residency differs between the final off/on orbit runs.

limitations: Streaming/publication epochs can reset history repeatedly on the orbit sweep; submitted/reset counts are recorded per capture. The retained baseline predates the committed temporal merge, so it is not an isolated T4c regression comparison.
Depth tolerance is an explicit 16*f32::EPSILON normalized-depth shortcut, not a measured metric disocclusion envelope.
Overlay shaders still read sampled jittered depth through the unjittered camera; a composed sampled/resolved depth policy and edge oracle remain open.
No arbitrary camera-cut token beyond the recorded view-mode/map/site tokens.
No object motion: rigid meshes (including static plants) and water reject history, so no foliage or ocean antialiasing benefit is claimed.
Static capture pairs and RGB deltas are not evidence of temporal stability, ghosting bounds, or subjective preference.
No upscaling, SDK, generated frame, simulation tick, stable-FPS or full client replacement claim.
